subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before OAuth starts, or should OpenClaw add gateway-owned credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: Both paths change where sensitive provider OAuth material may be acquired or moved, and automation should not choose that credential boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a clear instruction to run auth on the gateway host while preserving loopback/tunnel setups.

options.title: Forward credentials to the gateway
options.body: Design an authenticated gateway RPC or setup flow that moves provider auth material to the gateway store without consuming tokens locally first.

options.title: Warn but allow local writes
options.body: Keep the current permissive behavior with a warning, accepting that users can still consume provider OAuth material on the wrong host.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a clear instruction to run auth on the gateway host while preserving loopback/tunnel setups.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor already authored the focused maintainer repair direction for the exact remote-node auth guard.
